chapter_title: Concerning the Four Fathers; what they are like.
chapter_note: A remarkably pure body-cosmos correspondence teaching with minimal editorial overlay. The four-fold mapping (directive→Father, eyes→light ships, body→living soul, tongue→Jesus the Splendour) is systematic and complete. Both sides of every mapping stay within the cosmic system throughout. The only editorial material is the dialogue frame opening (¶1 attribution) and closing (¶9). The negative editorial fatigue score confirms substrate dominance increasing toward the chapter's end. 'Jesus the Splendour' functions as a cosmic emanation entity (the revealer principle) rather than a historical figure; the name may overlay an older cosmic revealer figure from the Persian tradition. The teaching structure itself—mapping four cosmic powers to four body faculties—is characteristic of the oldest correspondential substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Just as the corporeal body has limbs that are hidden, so it also has others that are visible. They can be seen upon it, they can be grasped and receive blows and wounds, whilst others can neither be grasped nor receive blows.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame attribution: 'Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples:' — formulaic opening introducing the teaching session.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The attribution formula 'Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples' is standard dialogue frame. The teaching that follows sets up the foundational body-analogy (hidden/visible, graspable/non-graspable) that structures the entire four-fold correspondence. The body analogy itself is substrate—it defines the two axes (visibility and vulnerability) that will map the four cosmic fathers.

paragraphs.core_text: So it is also with this entire greatness, as we resemble it. Some of it is hidden, whilst some of it is visible; some of it is far away from the blows and suffering, whilst some of it receives blows and wounds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Pivots from body to cosmic system ('this entire greatness'). 'As we resemble it' is a classical microcosm-macrocosm statement—the body IS the cosmic system in miniature. This is the correspondential thesis: the body's structure maps onto the cosmic structure. Both sides remain within the system. No editorial vocabulary detected.

paragraphs.core_text: Now, thus the directive of the body that lives within, hidden in the storehouses inside the body and unseen. So it is also how the Father, the God of truth, exists; as he too is hidden in his kingdom, not displayed before this outer desolation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First correspondence: directive faculty → Father. 'Storehouses inside the body' uses the correspondential 'storehouses' vocabulary found elsewhere in the substrate. 'Outer desolation' is a cosmic-geographical term for the realm of mixture. Both sides of the mapping are cosmic. The 'Now, thus' opening is a teaching connector, not an editorial bridge—it continues the systematic enumeration.

paragraphs.core_text: Thus, too, the body has two eyes that are visible and seen, and are even the body's source of illumination; so there are also these two light ships that shine and are seen in the entire universe and the whole of creation. The light has never been hidden, just like the two eyes of the body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second correspondence: two eyes → two light ships (sun and moon). 'Light ships' is systematic cosmic vocabulary. The mapping is precise: eyes illuminate the body / light ships illuminate the universe. Both sides stay within the cosmic system. The substrate vocabulary score (7.14) correctly flags 'light ships' as substrate terminology.

paragraphs.core_text: The living soul too is like this; it is established in apparent silence. In its apparent silence it is grasped and receives blows from these five fleshes, which destroy (the soul) and strike it. It can be likened to the mystery of the corporeal body, as it can be grasped and mastered, can receive blows and wounds.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third correspondence: body → living soul. 'Five fleshes' is a key substrate term for the five material kinds. 'Apparent silence' describes the soul's cosmic condition—present but passive, vulnerable. The substrate score (10.53) is the highest in the chapter, correctly reflecting 'living soul' and 'five fleshes' as diagnostic substrate vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.152⟩ Also, thus this tongue that speaks, proclaims, reprimands and reveals about everything happening in this body, inside and outside, also the considerations and bodily knowledges. The tongue, which is outside, makes it manifest. It also proclaims about the honour and shame of the body. And it speaks, unveiling the pain of the body that is sick from its sores.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Body-side of the fourth correspondence: the tongue's function. This paragraph describes WHAT the tongue is within the body—the faculty that reveals hidden and manifest conditions. The cosmic mapping (tongue → Jesus the Splendour) follows in ¶7. The two-paragraph structure (body-side, then cosmic-side) is characteristic of systematic correspondential exposition. Manuscript page marker ⟨p.152⟩ preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also what Jesus the Splendour is like, who shall be sent from the greatness. He manifests and reveals about everything, both the external and the internal, both what is above and what is below. Be it about the outer aeons that are hidden and not displayed, or about the ships of light that are seen: he is the one who unveils about them. He is also the one who reveals about their glory, and the greatness that dwells in them.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic-side of the fourth correspondence: tongue → Jesus the Splendour. 'Who shall be sent from the greatness' is emanation language—how a cosmic entity proceeds from a higher degree. 'Outer aeons,' 'ships of light,' 'the greatness' are all cosmic-system vocabulary. Both sides of the mapping stay within the system. 'Jesus the Splendour' functions here as a cosmic emanation entity (the revealer principle), not a historical figure; the name may overlay an older cosmic revealer from the Persian tradition. The substrate score (2.44) is low because the vocabulary is distributed rather than concentrated in diagnostic terms, but the content is entirely cosmic-correspondential.

paragraphs.core_text: And regarding this beating and wounding of the living soul, Jesus is the one who reveals it. He also preaches about (the soul) and its peace. He also reveals about its cleansing and healing.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Completes the fourth correspondence by linking the tongue/Jesus mapping back to the soul/body mapping: as the tongue reveals the body's sickness, so Jesus reveals the soul's suffering and healing. 'Living soul' is substrate vocabulary. 'Cleansing and healing' are cosmic-process terms describing the soul's restoration within the system. Both sides remain within the cosmic architecture.

'Behold, I have shown to you' is a first-person speaker-to-audience closure formula. The content that follows ('the power of revelation of these four fathers, and how each one of them has his appointed work, whether in secret or visible') is a back-reference summary of the teaching rather than new correspondential content. The four-fold teaching is already complete in ¶3-8. This paragraph wraps up the pedagogical session—a dialogue frame closure. The bridge connective flag correctly identifies this as non-substrate.
